description: Sujeeth Foundation domain ontology and governance configuration, including validated concepts used to associate approved external domains.

classes.name: Sujeeth Foundation
classes.definition: The nonprofit organization delivering the Career Circle Program and providing books to students.

classes.name: Partner
classes.definition: An institution working with Sujeeth Foundation through a Partnership.

classes.name: Partnership
classes.definition: A semester-specific relationship between Sujeeth Foundation and one Partner institution.

classes.name: Career Circle Program
classes.definition: The Foundation program delivered through Partnerships.

classes.name: Academic Period
classes.definition: The semester in which a Partnership operates.

classes.name: Circle
classes.definition: A cohort hosted by a Partnership and containing six individual Sessions.

classes.name: Session
classes.definition: One weekly meeting within a Circle.

classes.name: Week
classes.definition: One of the six program weeks.

classes.name: Student
classes.definition: A student participating in a Circle.

classes.name: Career Mentor
classes.definition: A volunteer who leads Sessions and guides Students.

classes.name: Volunteer
classes.definition: A person volunteering with the Foundation or a Partner.

classes.name: Community Manager
classes.definition: A role supporting coordination between a Partner and Volunteers; cannot lead a Circle.

classes.name: Resource
classes.definition: Learning material supporting one or more program Weeks.

classes.name: Book
classes.definition: A catalogued book that is also a Resource.

classes.name: Book Request
classes.definition: A Student request for a catalogued Book.

classes.name: Substitute Request
classes.definition: A request by a Mentor for another Volunteer to cover a Session.

classes.name: Onboarding Survey
classes.definition: The onboarding survey completed by a Student.

classes.name: Feedback Survey
classes.definition: The feedback survey completed by a Student.

classes.name: Presentation
classes.definition: A presentation or Sway resource associated with program content.

classes.name: Recording
classes.definition: A recording of a Session. The recording link is stored on a Circle Note (Dataverse table suj_circlenotes, column suj_note) and labeled by the meeting (suj_meeting).

classes.name: Agenda
classes.definition: The agenda for a program Week or Session.

classes.name: Spotlight
classes.definition: A feature highlighting one Volunteer.

classes.name: Testimonial
classes.definition: A quotation from one Student.

classes.name: Impact Report
classes.definition: A report describing Foundation impact.

classes.name: Donor
classes.definition: A person or organization making Donations to the Foundation.

classes.name: Donation
classes.definition: A contribution made to Sujeeth Foundation.

classes.name: Resume Resource
classes.definition: A learning resource that helps students create, improve, format, or tailor a resume or curriculum vitae for employment opportunities.

classes.name: Career Development
aliases: what do I want to be
classes.definition: Learning and activities that help a person explore career options, build professional skills, prepare for employment, and progress in a career.

classes.name: Leadership
classes.definition: The knowledge and practices involved in guiding, influencing, and supporting people or teams toward shared goals.

classes.name: Growth Mindset
classes.definition: The belief that abilities and skills can be developed through effort, learning, feedback, and practice.

classes.name: Grit
classes.definition: Perseverance and sustained commitment toward long-term goals despite challenges or setbacks.

classes.name: Purpose
classes.definition: A person's sense of meaning, direction, and motivation that informs goals and choices.

classes.name: Networking
classes.definition: Building and maintaining professional relationships that support learning, collaboration, and career opportunities.

classes.name: Innovation
classes.definition: Developing, testing, and applying new ideas or approaches to create value or solve problems.

classes.name: Motivation
classes.definition: The internal and external factors that initiate, direct, and sustain goal-oriented behavior.

classes.name: Appreciation
classes.definition: Recognizing and expressing the value of people, contributions, and positive experiences.

classes.name: Week 1
classes.definition: Week 1 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Self-Assessment. Understand strengths, goals, and growth areas; build trust and a personal narrative.

classes.name: Week 2
classes.definition: Week 2 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Research & Exploration. Explore industries, roles, and companies that fit your goals.

classes.name: Week 3
classes.definition: Week 3 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Resume & Preparation. Build a base resume and a LinkedIn profile that match your target roles.

classes.name: Week 4
classes.definition: Week 4 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Networking. Build professional relationships through generosity and visibility.

classes.name: Week 5
aliases: how many jobs should I apply to
classes.definition: Week 5 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Applications & Interviews. Choose an application strategy and tell your experience well in interviews.

classes.name: Week 6
classes.definition: Week 6 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Follow-up & Negotiation. Follow up after interviews, negotiate offers, and build relationships beyond transactions.

classes.name: Program Statistics
classes.definition: Counts and rates describing Foundation reach and results. The authoritative sources are sujeeth.org and topics.sujeeth.org; no other domain is.

classes.name: Circle Notes
classes.definition: Notes recorded about a Circle (Dataverse table suj_circlenotes). Each note holds a meeting label (suj_meeting) and a link (suj_note) to the Session's Recording.

classes.name: Portal Feedback
classes.definition: Feedback submitted about the student portal (Dataverse table suj_portalfeedback).

classes.name: Follow-up
classes.definition: Staying in touch after interviews and networking conversations in a way that builds the relationship (Week 6).

classes.name: Job Application Strategy
aliases: how many jobs to apply to
classes.definition: Choosing how many roles to apply to and how much to personalize each application (Week 5).

classes.name: Learning from Regret
classes.definition: Using regret as information for braver, more authentic career choices (Week 6).

classes.name: Salary Negotiation
classes.definition: Preparing for and conducting a conversation about pay and terms in a job offer.

classes.name: Interviewing
classes.definition: Preparing for and performing well in job interviews.

classes.name: LinkedIn Profile
classes.definition: Building a professional LinkedIn profile and presence as a student or early-career professional.

classes.name: Psychological Safety
classes.definition: A team climate where people can raise questions, ideas, and mistakes without fear of embarrassment or punishment.

classes.name: Vulnerability and Courage
classes.definition: Showing up honestly, taking risks, and handling fear of failure or judgment.

classes.name: Right Kind of Wrong
classes.definition: A framework for distinguishing kinds of failure and learning thoughtfully from setbacks by considering uncertainty, preventability, context, and consequences.

classes.name: Permission to Feel
classes.definition: A framework for noticing and naming emotions without judgment, exploring what they may signal about needs, concerns, or values, and using that awareness to choose a considered next step.

business_rules.rule: A Partnership represents a relationship between the Foundation and one Partner institution for one Academic Period.
A Partner may have multiple Partnerships in the same Academic Period.
Each Circle contains exactly six individual Sessions, one for each program Week.
A Community Manager cannot lead a Circle. A person serving separately as a Career Mentor may lead Sessions in that Mentor capacity.
A Student may request up to six distinct book titles. Cancelled Book Requests do not count toward the limit.
A Book Request references one catalogued Book and is associated with a Partnership for reporting only; the Partner is not involved in fulfillment.
A Substitute Request is made by a Mentor for one Session and is covered by another Volunteer.
Donations are made to the Foundation and are not associated with a Partner or Circle.
Program statistics come only from sujeeth.org and topics.sujeeth.org. Do not total them from Dataverse rows, and do not take them from Candid, third-party sites, or older documents.

Session Recordings are the links stored on Circle Notes (Dataverse table suj_circlenotes, column suj_note), labeled by suj_meeting and linked to a Circle through suj_circle. To find recordings, look up the Circle first, then read its notes.

suj_note is the Session Recording link, suj_meeting is the meeting label, and suj_circle links the note to its Circle.
Career Mentors are contact rows with suj_ismentor = true, linked to a Circle through the suj_circle field; employer is in jobtitle.
